step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 41-year-old male presenting with painful cervical lymphadenopathy and arthralgia

step5_concept_grounding: Suspected diagnosis of Chikungunya evaluated in patient with necrotizing lymphadenitis and arthralgia

evidence_items.source_quote: The chikungunya IgM antibody was not detected by serum IgM ELISA.

step10_contradiction_notes: Clinicians made an unconfirmed clinical diagnosis of chikungunya based on history and symptoms, but disease-specific serum IgM ELISA was explicitly negative (not detected), failing the gold standard laboratory evidence requirement.
rationale: A 41-year-old male with painful cervical lymphadenopathy, fever, and later polyarthralgia. While clinicians posited a clinical diagnosis based on symptoms, specific laboratory testing was explicitly negative: 'The chikungunya IgM antibody was not detected by serum IgM ELISA' (E0 refuting/contradicted evidence). Under strict gold-standard curation rules, supportive symptoms (E3) in the presence of a negative specific assay fail VPD criteria. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 38-year-old male with expanded dengue syndrome and small-medium-vessel vasculitis

rationale: A 38-year-old male diagnosed with expanded dengue syndrome and vasculitis. Diagnostic workup specifically evaluated Chikungunya as an infectious marker and yielded negative results (E0 refuting evidence), ruling out Chikungunya coinfection. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case 4; 12-year-old male with fever, rash, and subsequently confirmed rickettsiosis

step5_concept_grounding: Initial clinical diagnosis of Chikungunya evaluated and contradicted by negative testing

evidence_items.source_quote: On this occasion, samples were taken to confirm chikungunya, yielding negative results.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial presumptive clinical diagnosis of chikungunya without lab confirmation was contradicted by negative laboratory tests on day 10 and subsequent positive serology for Rickettsia typhi.
rationale: A 12-year-old male was initially presumptively diagnosed with chikungunya clinically without testing. Upon re-evaluation on day 10, laboratory testing was performed to confirm chikungunya and yielded negative results (E0 contradictory evidence). The patient was subsequently confirmed to have Rickettsia typhi infection. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 40-year-old female returned traveler from Philippines with Chikungunya arthritis

step5_concept_grounding: Diagnosis of Chikungunya arthritis developing into chronic phase

evidence_items.source_quote: This time CHIKV-IgM was detected and CHIKV-polyvalent-antibody titre had risen from 1 : <10 to 1 : 1280. The first CHIKV-IgM negative sample was reexamined and was CHIKV-PCR positive (Table 1).

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial acute CHIKV-IgM test was negative due to early sampling window, but resolved with convalescent seroconversion (titer rise to 1:1280) and acute sample retrospective PCR positivity.
rationale: A 40-year-old female traveler returned with acute fever and severe symmetrical polyarthritis. Initial acute IgM was negative, but convalescent testing demonstrated IgM seroconversion with antibody titer rising to 1:1280, and the initial sample was confirmed CHIKV-PCR positive (E1 confirmatory molecular evidence). Contradiction fully resolved. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case presentation; 27-year-old female traveler returning from Costa Rica to Croatia with imported Chikungunya fever

step10_contradiction_notes: RT-PCR at day 20 was negative, which is expected due to clearance of viremia beyond the acute phase, while disease-specific IgM and high-titer IgG (1:10,000) confirmed chronic chikungunya without cross-reactivity to other arboviruses.
rationale: A 27-year-old female returning from Costa Rica developed acute fever, rash, and persistent polyarthralgias. Serology on day 20 revealed high-titer CHIKV IgM (1:100) and IgG (1:10,000) by IFA (E2 evidence) with exclusion of cross-reactivity against Zika, dengue, West Nile, Usutu, and yellow fever. RT-PCR negativity at day 20 reflects expected post-viremic timing. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report; 31-year-old female with SLE developing longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (neuro-chikungunya)

rationale: A 31-year-old female with SLE developed acute ascending tetraparesis, fever, arthritis, and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis.
